text: When swimming, it's important to focus on the proper kicking technique to maintain a streamline position and propel yourself forward. For most swimmers, this involves engaging their glutes, hamstrings, and quadriceps, while keeping their heels on the ground and their toes pointed forward. Once the body is efficiently kicking, the swimmer then turns their attention to breathing. Most swimmers learn to breathe every three to five strokes, following a pattern called the 3-2-1 breathing technique. This involves taking a breath on the third stroke, followed by two on the fourth, one on the fifth, and finally holding or exhaling on the sixth stroke before resuming the kicking motion. This sequence ensures adequate breathing without interrupting the continuous forward motion essential to effective swimming. The combination of kicking and breathing allows swimmers to sustain a steady and powerful stroke, which is the foundation of efficient swimming.
